hints: Rather than building every string of brackets and checking it later, ask: at each step, when is adding ( allowed, and when is adding ) allowed?
Backtrack while tracking open and close counts. Add ( if open < n; add ) only if close < open. Every finished string is then balanced.

1. Start with an empty StringBuilder, open = close = 0.
  2. If length is 2n, save the string.
  3. If open < n: append (, recurse with open+1, delete it.
  4. If close < open: append ), recurse with close+1, delete it.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Generate all 2<sup>2n</sup> strings of brackets and keep the balanced ones.

approaches.name: Optimal: constrained backtracking
approaches.idea: Only ever extend with a legal bracket, so every leaf is a valid answer (the n-th Catalan number of them).

explain: For n = 2: start with (. Next we may add ( (giving ((, which can only close as (())) or ) (giving (), then ( and ) → ()()). A string can never start with ) because close < open fails. The invariant close ≤ open ≤ n holds at every step, so no prefix is ever unbalanced, and we get exactly 2 strings.
recognize: 'Generate every balanced/valid string of n pairs' → backtracking with open/close counters as the constraint.
